tagline: From a Revolutionary battlefield to a town of fifty-five.
intro: From Kings Mountain National Military Park near Bethany, SC 161 runs into York, and a string of state roads carries the byway on through McConnells to the Bullock Creek community, then through Sharon and Hickory Grove to Smyrna, all one contiguous route.

Smyrna, the end of the line, counted 55 people at the 2020 census. It took its name from the Smyrna Associate Reformed Presbyterian Church, which had served the neighborhood for fifty years before the town was incorporated in 1895.

moments.title: Kings Mountain National Military Park
moments.text: Here on October 7, 1780, the Patriots destroyed the left wing of Cornwallis's army in the battle Thomas Jefferson called the turn of the tide of success.

moments.title: Historic Brattonsville
moments.text: Down a side road of nearly two miles stand the Bratton family houses, the oldest a 1776 log house hidden under later clapboards, where scenes of the 2000 film The Patriot were shot.

moments.title: Sharon
moments.text: The old Hill's Mercantile, built around 1900 of bricks fired right on the site, is the tallest building in the southwestern part of the county.
